title: NXIVM (Keith Raniere) — sex trafficking and organized crime
summary: NXIVM Corporation, founded by Keith Raniere, operated under the cover of a self-help and professional-development company. Federal investigations revealed an elaborate structure of coercive control, exploitation of female members, enforced debt bondage, and organized crime. Raniere and key associates were convicted in 2019–2021 on charges including racketeering, sex trafficking, forced labor, and financial crimes. The organization operated in the United States (NY, CA) and internationally (Mexico, Canada). Sayari and legal records show risk concentrated on individual leaders rather than the corporate shell, illustrating how small-business screening must traverse to beneficial owners.

journey.note: NXIVM headquarters. Marketed as self-help and professional development courses to attract members.
Inner circle (DOS — 'Dominus Obsequious Sororium') recruited women into coercive system with collateral, debt, and isolation.

Women confined to compounds, subjected to psychological manipulation, coerced into commercial sex acts, branded with Raniere's initials, held by manipulated 'collateral' (secrets, recordings, photos).
US District Court, Eastern District of New York. Raniere convicted June 19, 2019; sentenced to 120 years October 27, 2020. Multiple co-conspirators convicted or pleaded guilty 2019–2021.

lures.quote_or_description: Women in DOS (inner circle) were isolated from family and friends, forbidden to associate outside the group, and monitored constantly. Raniere dictated who could speak to whom.

Members were coerced into creating 'collateral' — secrets, recordings, naked photos — that was used as leverage to keep them in the organization and compliant with orders, including labor and sex acts.
Women paid thousands of dollars in course fees and 'coaching' payments to Raniere and his inner circle. Payments were extracted under psychological coercion.
Victims were threatened with exposure of collateral (naked photos, personal secrets) if they tried to leave or disclosed the organization's activities.
